# Model and source

Koele 2024 is a clinical-trial-simulation study of how much power a 14-day
phase IIa (early bactericidal activity) trial in pulmonary tuberculosis has
to identify an exposure-response relationship, depending on whether the
bacterial load is measured as colony-forming units (CFU), as time to
positivity (TTP) in liquid culture, or as both. It contributes five models:

* `Koele_2024_rifampicin_bacterialload` -- the joint bilinear CFU + TTP
  model fitted to the PanACEA HIGHRIF1 trial of high-dose rifampicin
  (Table 2, 'Estimate' column). This is the paper's only fitted model.
* `Koele_2024_TB_drugA`, `Koele_2024_TB_drugB`, `Koele_2024_TB_drugC`,
  `Koele_2024_TB_drugD` -- the simulation models for the four HYPOTHETICAL
  drugs (Table 2, 'Simulation value' column): a one-compartment PK model
  whose individual daily AUC0-24 drives the slopes of the HIGHRIF1
  bacterial-load model through an Emax relationship.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Koele_2024_rifampicin_bacterialload"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13089>

The bacterial load follows the bilinear form of Equation 1, with one node
shared by both endpoints:

$$
\text{load}(t) =
\begin{cases}
\text{Intercept} \mp \text{Slope}_1 \, t & t \le \text{node} \\
\text{load}(\text{node}) \mp \text{Slope}_2 \, (t - \text{node}) & t > \text{node}
\end{cases}
$$

where CFU declines (minus) and TTP rises (plus); both are on the log10
scale. In the hypothetical-drug models each slope is
$\text{Slope}_i = E_{\max,i} \cdot \text{AUC}_{0-24} / (\text{EC}_{50} + \text{AUC}_{0-24}) \cdot e^{\eta_i}$
(Equation 2), with one EC50 shared by all slopes.

# Population

The HIGHRIF1 model was developed on 99 adults with sputum-smear-positive
pulmonary tuberculosis who received rifampicin 10 to 50 mg/kg daily in
separate dose groups, as monotherapy for 7 days followed by 7 days with
standard-dose isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol added. Sputum was
collected on Days 0-7, 9 and 14 and cultured in duplicate by both methods,
giving 1959 CFU and 1968 TTP measurements, of which 151 (7.7%) CFU and
22 (1.1%) TTP samples were culture-negative (Koele 2024 Methods and
Results, 'Pharmacodynamic model'). Koele 2024 does not tabulate
demographics; they are in the primary HIGHRIF1 publications.

The hypothetical-drug models describe virtual patients: 1000 per drug
(250 at each of four dose levels, 1x to 4x a base daily dose) with no
covariates.

```{r population}
str(readModelDb("Koele_2024_rifampicin_bacterialload")()$population)
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The table
collects them. CV% values were converted to variances with
$\omega^2 = \log(1 + \text{CV}^2)$, per the Table 2 footnote
('CV% was calculated as sqrt(exp(OMEGA2) - 1)'), and correlations to
covariances with $r \sqrt{\omega_1^2 \omega_2^2}$.

| Quantity | HIGHRIF1 fit | Hypothetical drugs | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline CFU (log10 CFU/mL) | 5.92 | 5.92 | Table 2 |
| Baseline TTP (log10 h) | 2.02 | 2.02 | Table 2 |
| Slope 1 CFU (log10 CFU/mL/h) | 0.0141 | Emax A 0.0329, B 0.0219, C 0.0110, D 0 | Table 2 |
| Slope 1 TTP (log10 h/h) | 0.00353 | Emax A 0.0056, B 0.0037, C 0.0019, D 0 | Table 2 |
| Slope 2 CFU (log10 CFU/mL/h) | 0.00662 | Emax A 0.00550, B 0.00370, C 0.00180, D 0.0120 | Table 2 |
| Slope 2 TTP (log10 h/h) | 0.000910 | Emax A 0.00093, B 0.00063, C 0.0003, D 0.00203 | Table 2 |
| Node (h) | 62.1 | A-C 62.1, D 144.0 | Table 2 |
| EC50 (mg*h/L) | n/a | low 5.0 (default), high 25.0 | Table 2 |
| CL (L/h), V (L), IIV CL | n/a | 10.0, 40.0, 30% CV | Table 2; Methods 'Pharmacokinetic model' |
| IIV baseline CFU / TTP, correlation | 15.4%, 5.5%, -71.5% | same | Table 2 |
| IIV slope 1 CFU / TTP, correlation | 58.3%, 30.9%, 94.1% | same (not in drug D) | Table 2 |
| IIV slope 2 CFU / TTP, correlation | 74.1%, 47.2%, 63.4% | same | Table 2 |
| Additive error CFU / TTP | 0.334, 0.00667 (variances; SD = square root) | same | Table 2; see 'Residual-error scale' |
| Bilinear structure, shared node | Equation 1 | Equation 1 | Methods; Supplementary File S1 $PRED |
| Emax on all four slopes, shared EC50 | n/a | Equation 2 | Methods; Supplementary File S1 $PRED |
| Log-normal IIV (THETA * EXP(ETA)) | yes | yes | Methods; Supplementary File S1 $PRED |
| Baseline chance of a negative culture | CFU 6.4%, TTP 0.35% | same | Table 2; Supplementary File S1 (PBAC) |
| LLOQ CFU / ULOQ TTP | 1 log10 CFU/mL / 3.003641 log10 h | same | Methods; Supplementary File S1 |

# Part 1 -- the HIGHRIF1 rifampicin model

## Typical-value check

The typical prediction is a closed-form function of the Table 2 values, so
the solved model must reproduce it to numerical precision.

```{r rif-typical}
mod_rif <- readModelDb("Koele_2024_rifampicin_bacterialload")
days <- c(0:7, 9, 14)
ev_typ <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = days * 24, evid = 0L, amt = 0, dvid = 1L)
typ_rif <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_rif), ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame")

bilinear <- function(t, e0, s1, s2, node, sign) {
  e0 + sign * (s1 * pmin(t, node) + s2 * pmax(t - node, 0))
}
closed <- data.frame(
  day = days,
  cfu_closed = bilinear(days * 24, 5.92, 0.0141, 0.00662, 62.1, -1),
  ttp_closed = bilinear(days * 24, 2.02, 0.00353, 0.000910, 62.1, +1)
)
chk_rif <- cbind(closed, cfu_model = typ_rif$log_cfu, ttp_model = typ_rif$log_ttp)
knitr::kable(chk_rif, digits = 4, caption = "Typical log10 CFU/mL and log10 TTP (h): model vs closed form.")
stopifnot(
  max(abs(chk_rif$cfu_model - chk_rif$cfu_closed)) < 1e-8,
  max(abs(chk_rif$ttp_model - chk_rif$ttp_closed)) < 1e-8
)
```

## Visual predictive check (Figure 1)

Figure 1 is a prediction-corrected VPC with the proportion of culture-negative
samples underneath. Culture negativity is simulated as in Supplementary
File S1: a sample is negative if the simulated value falls below the CFU
LLOQ (1 log10 CFU/mL) or above the TTP ULOQ (log10 of 42 days in hours,
3.003641 in the control stream), or -- independently of the bacterial load --
with the baseline chance that reflects the sensitivity of the culture method
(6.4% for CFU, 0.35% for TTP).

```{r rif-vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2024)
set.seed(2024)
n_rif <- 200L
ev_rif <- expand.grid(id = seq_len(n_rif), time = days * 24, dvid = 1:2) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dvid) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0)
sim_rif <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_rif, ev_rif, keep = "dvid", returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    day = time / 24,
    endpoint = ifelse(dvid == 1, "CFU (log10 CFU/mL)", "TTP (log10 h)"),
    pbac = ifelse(dvid == 1, 0.064, 0.0035),
    censored = ifelse(dvid == 1, sim < 1, sim > 3.003641),
    negative = censored | (stats::runif(dplyr::n()) < pbac)
  )

vpc_rif <- sim_rif |>
  dplyr::group_by(endpoint, day) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p025 = quantile(sim[!negative], 0.025),
    p50 = median(sim[!negative]),
    p975 = quantile(sim[!negative], 0.975),
    prop_negative = mean(negative),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(sim_rif |> dplyr::filter(!negative), aes(day, sim)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.7, colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(data = vpc_rif, aes(y = p50), colour = "red") +
  geom_line(data = vpc_rif, aes(y = p025), colour = "red", linetype = 2) +
  geom_line(data = vpc_rif, aes(y = p975), colour = "red", linetype = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of treatment (days)", y = NULL,
    title = "Simulated HIGHRIF1 bacterial load, culture-positive samples",
    caption = "Replicates the layout of Figure 1 of Koele 2024 (median and 2.5th/97.5th percentiles)."
  )
```

The percentiles read off Figure 1 (the centres of the authors' simulated
prediction intervals) are compared with the simulation below. TTP agrees
within about 0.05 log10 h. For CFU the simulated median runs 0.1-0.25
log10 CFU/mL below the authors' band, and from Day 7 on the simulated
97.5th percentile runs about 0.3-0.7 below it (0.3-0.5 in a 5000-subject
run, so not only sampling noise); see 'Assumptions and deviations'.

```{r rif-vpc-table}
fig1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~endpoint,            ~day, ~fig1_p50, ~fig1_p975,
  "CFU (log10 CFU/mL)",  0,   6.1,       8.2,
  "CFU (log10 CFU/mL)",  7,   4.4,       7.1,
  "CFU (log10 CFU/mL)", 14,   3.5,       6.5,
  "TTP (log10 h)",       0,   2.00,      2.34,
  "TTP (log10 h)",       7,   2.35,      2.68,
  "TTP (log10 h)",      14,   2.50,      2.85
)
fig1 |>
  dplyr::left_join(vpc_rif, by = c("endpoint", "day")) |>
  dplyr::select(endpoint, day, fig1_p50, p50, fig1_p975, p975) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Endpoint" = endpoint, "Day" = day,
    "Median, Figure 1" = fig1_p50, "Median, simulated" = p50,
    "97.5th, Figure 1" = fig1_p975, "97.5th, simulated" = p975
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Figure 1 prediction-interval centres (digitised) vs this simulation, culture-positive samples.")
```

The culture-negative proportions are not affected by prediction correction,
so they are the sharper check of the residual-error and censoring structure.
Figure 1 shows roughly 5% of CFU samples negative on Day 0 rising to about
22% on Day 14, and TTP rising from 0% to about 5%.

```{r rif-negative}
neg_tab <- vpc_rif |>
  dplyr::select(endpoint, day, prop_negative) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = endpoint, values_from = prop_negative)
knitr::kable(neg_tab, digits = 3, caption = "Simulated proportion of culture-negative samples by day (Figure 1 lower panels).")

neg_cfu <- vpc_rif |> dplyr::filter(endpoint == "CFU (log10 CFU/mL)")
neg_overall <- sim_rif |> dplyr::group_by(endpoint) |> dplyr::summarise(prop = mean(negative))
knitr::kable(neg_overall, digits = 3, caption = "Overall simulated culture-negative proportion; observed 7.7% (CFU) and 1.1% (TTP).")
stopifnot(
  # Day 14: Figure 1 shows about 22% (prediction band ~15-30%). With 200
  # subjects the simulated proportion has a standard error of ~3%.
  abs(neg_cfu$prop_negative[neg_cfu$day == 14] - 0.22) < 0.10,
  # Days 0-7 sit near the 6.4% baseline chance in both Figure 1 and here.
  abs(median(neg_cfu$prop_negative[neg_cfu$day <= 7]) - 0.064) < 0.04
)
```

## Residual-error scale

Table 2 prints the additive errors as 0.334 (CFU) and 0.00667 (TTP) with
log10 units, which reads like standard deviations. They are encoded as
variances (SD = 0.578 and 0.0817). The Day-0 width of Figure 1's 95%
prediction interval separates the two readings, because at Day 0 only the
baseline variability and the residual error contribute. The intervals
digitised from Figure 1 are 3.74-8.17 log10 CFU/mL (width 4.43) and
1.80-2.34 log10 h (width 0.53).

```{r residual-scale}
set.seed(1)
day0_width <- function(e0, cv, resid_sd, n = 1e5) {
  y <- e0 * exp(stats::rnorm(n, 0, sqrt(log(1 + cv^2)))) + stats::rnorm(n, 0, resid_sd)
  unname(diff(quantile(y, c(0.025, 0.975))))
}
widths <- data.frame(
  endpoint = c("CFU", "TTP"),
  figure1 = c(4.43, 0.53),
  variance_reading = c(day0_width(5.92, 0.154, sqrt(0.334)), day0_width(2.02, 0.055, sqrt(0.00667))),
  sd_reading = c(day0_width(5.92, 0.154, 0.334), day0_width(2.02, 0.055, 0.00667))
)
knitr::kable(widths, digits = 3, caption = "Day-0 95% prediction-interval width: Figure 1 vs the two readings of Table 2.")
stopifnot(all(abs(widths$variance_reading - widths$figure1) < abs(widths$sd_reading - widths$figure1)))
```

# Part 2 -- the hypothetical-drug simulation models

## Exposure and dose

The paper gives the PK constants but not the base daily dose. Each slope
depends on the dose only through $\text{AUC}_{0-24} = \text{dose}/\text{CL}$,
and Figure 2 (typical CFU profiles at 1x-4x) pins it: the 1x, 2x and 4x
curves for drug A all imply a typical 1x AUC0-24 of 10 mg*h/L, i.e. a
base dose of 100 mg at CL = 10 L/h. It is consistent with the Methods,
which place the low EC50 (5.0) below the average 1x exposure (10) and the
high EC50 (25) below the average 3x exposure (30).

```{r hyp-setup}
drug_models <- c(
  A = "Koele_2024_TB_drugA", B = "Koele_2024_TB_drugB",
  C = "Koele_2024_TB_drugC", D = "Koele_2024_TB_drugD"
)
base_dose <- 100 # mg; back-solved from Figure 2
dose_levels <- c(`1x` = 1, `2x` = 2, `3x` = 3, `4x` = 4)

make_events <- function(n, multiple, obs_times, id_offset = 0L) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = 24 * (0:13)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = base_dose * multiple, evid = 1L, dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs_rows <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
    dplyr::mutate(cmt = "central", dose_level = names(dose_levels)[multiple]) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
```

## Typical CFU profiles (Figure 2) and TTP profiles (Figure S1a)

```{r figure-2}
typ_events <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(dose_levels), function(i) {
  make_events(1L, i, obs_times = 0:336, id_offset = i - 1L)
}))
typ_hyp <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(drug_models), function(d) {
  m <- rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb(drug_models[[d]]))
  rxode2::rxSolve(m, typ_events, keep = "dose_level", returnType = "data.frame", useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(drug = paste("Drug", d))
}))

ggplot(typ_hyp, aes(time / 24, log_cfu, colour = dose_level)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~drug) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of treatment (days)", y = "Log10 CFU/mL", colour = "Dose",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Koele 2024 (low EC50, base dose 100 mg)."
  )

ggplot(typ_hyp, aes(time / 24, log_ttp, colour = dose_level)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~drug) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of treatment (days)", y = "Log10 TTP (h)", colour = "Dose",
    caption = "Replicates Figure S1a of Koele 2024 (low EC50, base dose 100 mg)."
  )
```

The Day-14 end points of the 16 Figure 2 curves were digitised by the
maintainers from the published figure (reading precision about 0.03 log10).
The typical-value simulation reproduces all of them.

```{r figure-2-check}
fig2_day14 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug,    ~dose_level, ~fig2,
  "Drug A", "1x", 3.56, "Drug A", "2x", 3.09, "Drug A", "3x", 2.89, "Drug A", "4x", 2.80,
  "Drug B", "1x", 4.34, "Drug B", "2x", 4.05, "Drug B", "3x", 3.92, "Drug B", "4x", 3.83,
  "Drug C", "1x", 5.14, "Drug C", "2x", 4.99, "Drug C", "3x", 4.92, "Drug C", "4x", 4.89,
  "Drug D", "1x", 4.39, "Drug D", "2x", 4.10, "Drug D", "3x", 3.97, "Drug D", "4x", 3.90
)
chk_fig2 <- typ_hyp |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 336) |>
  dplyr::select(drug, dose_level, log_cfu) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig2_day14, by = c("drug", "dose_level")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(diff = log_cfu - fig2)
chk_fig2 |>
  dplyr::rename("Drug" = drug, "Dose" = dose_level, "Simulated" = log_cfu, "Figure 2" = fig2, "Difference" = diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Typical log10 CFU/mL on Day 14: simulation vs Figure 2.")
stopifnot(nrow(chk_fig2) == 16L, max(abs(chk_fig2$diff)) < 0.1)
```

The Methods describe drug A as giving at most a 3 log10 CFU/mL decrease
over 14 days, drug B 2, drug C 1, and drug D a maximum similar to drug B.
At the highest (4x) dose the typical decreases are:

```{r max-decline}
typ_hyp |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 336, dose_level == "4x") |>
  dplyr::transmute(Drug = drug, `Decrease over 14 days, 4x dose (log10 CFU/mL)` = 5.92 - log_cfu) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

## High EC50 scenario (Figures S1b and S1c)

The high-EC50 scenario is the same model with `lec50 = log(25)`.

```{r high-ec50}
typ_high <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(drug_models), function(d) {
  m <- rxode2::zeroRe(readModelDb(drug_models[[d]])) |> rxode2::ini(lec50 = log(25))
  rxode2::rxSolve(m, typ_events, keep = "dose_level", returnType = "data.frame", useLinCmt = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(drug = paste("Drug", d))
}))
typ_high |>
  dplyr::select(drug, dose_level, time, log_cfu, log_ttp) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(log_cfu, log_ttp), names_to = "endpoint") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, value, colour = dose_level, linetype = drug)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~endpoint, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of treatment (days)", y = NULL, colour = "Dose", linetype = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figures S1b and S1c of Koele 2024 (high EC50)."
  )

# With EC50 = 25 the 1x dose reaches only 10 / 35 of the maximum slope, so
# the dose levels spread further apart than at the low EC50.
spread <- function(x) {
  d14 <- x |> dplyr::filter(time == 336, drug == "Drug B")
  d14$log_cfu[d14$dose_level == "1x"] - d14$log_cfu[d14$dose_level == "4x"]
}
c(low_ec50 = spread(typ_hyp), high_ec50 = spread(typ_high))
```

## Stochastic simulation, drug B (reference scenario)

Drug B with the low EC50 is the reference for the paper's design and
sensitivity analyses. The clinical trial simulations sampled CFU and TTP on
Days 0-5, 7, 9 and 14; a dense grid over the last dosing interval
(Days 13-14) is added for the NCA below.

```{r drugB-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(13089)
n_arm <- 100L
pd_times <- c(0:5, 7, 9, 14) * 24
pk_times <- seq(312, 336, by = 0.5)
ev_b <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(dose_levels), function(i) {
  make_events(n_arm, i, obs_times = sort(unique(c(pd_times, pk_times))), id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_arm)
}))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_b[, c("id", "time", "evid")])))
sim_b <- rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb("Koele_2024_TB_drugB"), ev_b,
  keep = "dose_level", returnType = "data.frame", useLinCmt = FALSE
)

sim_b |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% pd_times) |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose_level, day = time / 24) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(log_cfu, 0.05), p50 = median(log_cfu), p95 = quantile(log_cfu, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(day, p50, colour = dose_level, fill = dose_level)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.1, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Time after start of treatment (days)", y = "Log10 CFU/mL (individual prediction)",
    colour = "Dose", fill = "Dose",
    caption = "Drug B, low EC50: median and 90% interval of individual predictions, 100 virtual patients per dose."
  )
```

## PKNCA validation of the exposure driver

The bacterial-load slopes are driven by `auc24 = dose / CL`, the steady-state
AUC0-24 of a one-compartment model. PKNCA computes the AUC over the last
dosing interval of the simulated concentrations, which must agree with it
subject by subject.

```{r pknca}
conc_b <- sim_b |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 312, !is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, dose_level)
dose_b <- ev_b |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1, time == 312) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, dose_level)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_b, Cc ~ time | dose_level + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_b, amt ~ time | dose_level + id, route = "intravascular")
intervals <- data.frame(start = 312, end = 336, cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_b <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_b$result) |>
  dplyr::select(id, dose_level, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
auc_model <- sim_b |>
  dplyr::filter(time == 336) |>
  dplyr::select(id, auc24)
chk_auc <- dplyr::inner_join(nca_wide, auc_model, by = "id") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auclast - auc24) / auc24)

nca_summary <- chk_auc |>
  dplyr::group_by(dose_level) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    cmax_median = median(cmax),
    auc_nca_median = median(auclast),
    auc_model_median = median(auc24),
    typical_auc = base_dose * dose_levels[[dose_level[1]]] / 10,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
nca_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose" = dose_level,
    "Cmax, median (mg/L)" = cmax_median,
    "AUC0-24 by PKNCA, median (mg*h/L)" = auc_nca_median,
    "auc24 = dose/CL, median (mg*h/L)" = auc_model_median,
    "Typical dose/CL (mg*h/L)" = typical_auc
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Day-14 NCA of drug B by dose level (100 virtual patients each).")

stopifnot(
  # Same drawn CL on both sides: only the trapezoid error of the 0.5 h grid
  # separates them.
  abs(median(chk_auc$pct_diff)) < 1,
  quantile(abs(chk_auc$pct_diff), 0.9) < 2,
  # Methods: low EC50 (5.0) below the average 1x exposure, high EC50 (25)
  # below the average 3x exposure.
  nca_summary$auc_nca_median[nca_summary$dose_level == "1x"] > 5,
  nca_summary$auc_nca_median[nca_summary$dose_level == "3x"] > 25
)
```

Koele 2024 reports no NCA for the hypothetical drugs, so there is no
published table to compare against; the check above validates the exposure
metric that drives the model.

# What is not reproduced

The paper's main results (Table 3, Figures 3 and 4, Figures S2-S4) are
statistical powers from Monte-Carlo mapped power analysis: every simulated
trial is re-fitted with the full Emax model and the reduced constant-slope
model (Equation 3), and the likelihood-ratio test is evaluated over 10,000
replicates. That needs re-estimation in NONMEM or nlmixr2 and is outside the
scope of a validation article. The misspecified linear exposure-response
model (Equation 4) is an analysis model only, with no reported estimates,
and is not packaged.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual-error scale.** Table 2 prints the additive errors as 0.334
  log10 CFU/mL and 0.00667 log10 h. They are treated as $SIGMA variances
  and encoded as SDs of 0.578 and 0.0817: the Day-0 width of the Figure 1
  prediction intervals matches the variance reading (see above), an SD of
  0.00667 log10 h would be an implausible 1.5% replicate CV for TTP, and the
  same group's BTZ-043 model (Koele 2025, built with the same methods)
  printed $SIGMA variances of 0.30-0.32 for CFU and 0.0035-0.0043 for TTP.
* **Residual correlations not encoded.** The model has one residual per
  endpoint. The correlation between the CFU and TTP additive errors
  (-47.4%) and the correlations between duplicate-sample replicate errors
  (CFU 90.3%, TTP 82.7%) are not represented, because nlmixr2lib has no
  idiomatic residual correlation across outputs or replicates. Marginal
  distributions are unaffected.
* **Culture-negative likelihood.** The M3 handling of culture-negative
  samples and the baseline chance of a negative culture (PBAC = 6.4% CFU,
  0.35% TTP) belong to the likelihood, not the structural model, and are
  reproduced in this article's simulation code rather than in the model
  files. To fit the models to data with culture-negative samples, use
  nlmixr2's censoring columns (`CENS`, `LIMIT`).
* **IIV form.** Equation 2 is printed as `* (1 + IIV)`, but the Methods
  ('Individual baseline bacterial load and slope were assumed to be
  log-normally distributed'), the Table 2 CV formula and the
  Supplementary File S1 code (`THETA * EXP(ETA)`) all use exponential
  variability, which is what is encoded.
* **Supplementary File S1 $THETA comments.** The $THETA comment labels
  (EC50 as THETA 7) do not match the $PRED code (EC50 as THETA 5, shared by
  CFU and TTP). The models follow the $PRED code.
* **ULOQ.** The control stream sets the TTP ULOQ to 3.003641; log10 of
  42 days in hours is 3.003461. The difference is immaterial and the
  control-stream value is used here.
* **Base dose.** The base daily dose of the hypothetical drugs is not
  stated; 100 mg (typical AUC0-24 10 mg*h/L at CL 10 L/h) was back-solved
  by the maintainers from Figure 2 and reproduces all 16 of its curves.
* **PK route.** The PK model is described by CL and V only. The dose is put
  into `central`; the route does not change AUC0-24, which is all the PD
  uses.
* **Drug D node.** The Methods describe drug D's onset as 'after 7 days',
  but Table 2 (node 144 h) and Figure 2d both place it at Day 6; 144 h is
  used. Drug D has no first-phase slope (Table 2: 'D: 0'), so its model
  omits the slope-1 parameters and their variability.
* **Estimation status.** The hypothetical-drug PK constants are wrapped in
  `fixed()` because the authors never estimated them (the analysis model
  takes AUC0-24 as data). The PD values are left unfixed because the
  authors re-estimated the PD model on every simulated trial.
* **pcVPC differences.** The TTP percentiles and the culture-negative
  proportions agree with Figure 1. For CFU, the simulated median sits
  0.1-0.25 log10 below the centre of the authors' median band, and from
  Day 7 on the simulated 97.5th percentile sits 0.3-0.5 log10 below
  theirs (5000-subject run), i.e. the authors' upper CFU tail declines
  more slowly than the Table 2 variabilities produce here. Prediction
  correction, the censoring rule applied in the authors' VPC and the exact
  sampling times of the baseline samples cannot be reconstructed from the
  paper, and no reading of Table 2 that changes the slope variabilities is
  supported by the text, so the parameters are kept as printed and the VPC
  percentiles are reported but not used as a gate.
* **Errata.** No correction notice for Koele 2024 was found (Crossref and
  Europe PMC, checked 2026-10-29).
